These tests reject those simple routes only; they do not prove every hand-service maneuver impossible. The real cover also carries a welded vent, pump supports, tool cradles and a hardware tray, so a full service sequence must identify what is disconnected or removed.
evidence.repair: Define and collision-check a practical washout service sequence with lid-mounted equipment, cable/hose disconnects and handling clearance. If that needs pan removal, state it. Otherwise introduce a suitable service hatch or a structurally justified removable obstruction, then rerun the assembled route.

evidence.title: Drained-level guard has only 0.672 mm clearance to the pan floor
evidence.detail: The PAN_EMPTY guard is nominally collision-free, but its floor sits less than 0.7 mm above the sloped welded pan at the closest point. No guard/floor fabrication, flatness, welding or debris tolerance is allocated. The wet-calibrated float is not a bone-dry detector, and raising this carrier changes its trip relation. A zero-interference result alone is insufficient to release this near-floor guard.

evidence.title: Pan guards are outside center travel but very close to its right edge

This audit does not assert a torch collision because the actual cutter/torch interface is not established.

evidence.title: Whole-frame rigidity and support stability remain unverified
evidence.detail: The design has a real two-inch tube frame, five braces and six custom screw feet, but the supplied strength screen treats ideal members and excludes joint rotation, gusset bending and complete-frame flexibility. Lowering the front upper tie removes the front high-level brace path; the documentation itself says racking must pass through the rear/side braces and connections. The 650 kg design mass is an assumption, and the foot check is axial compression plus gross pad pressure. No complete machine load/deflection budget, assembled mass/center-of-gravity or anchorage/floor acceptance is shown. Sand is correctly not credited as added elastic stiffness.
evidence.repair: Set a required tool-to-work deflection budget and actual load cases, then check the assembled frame, connections, feet and support surface with appropriate analysis and/or a measured load test. Determine mass/center of gravity for router/plasma/service configurations and close anchoring/leveling requirements. Preserve the member-screen qualification.

findings.title: Cabinet access is plausible but an enclosure block does not prove service clearance
findings.required_action: Use the selected enclosure drawing to model or conservatively bound the door/hinges/latch and removable panel; verify access, transfer holes, cable bend/entry spaces and thermal layout. Retain packaging-envelope release status until closed.

evidence.title: Cabinet access is plausible but an enclosure block does not prove service clearance
evidence.detail: The upright front location improves access and the nominal top/bottom door projection clears the frame. However the purchase is represented by a solid external envelope, not its door, hinges, latch, mounting panel or cable entries. The nominal cage holes are transfer-drilled, cable routes and VFD heat rejection are unreleased, and no door/tool-access sweep is represented. These known gaps must remain visible despite the package-status claim that cabinet service is resolved.
evidence.repair: Use the selected enclosure drawing to model or conservatively bound the door/hinges/latch and removable panel; verify access, transfer holes, cable bend/entry spaces and thermal layout. Retain packaging-envelope release status until closed.
